questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. When you speak, there are gestures and body language that ______ your words.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

When you speak, there are gestures and body language that ______ your words.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'accompany.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is saying when we speak, our gestures and body language go together with our words.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'accompany'.
  • The word 'accompany' means anything that goes together well with something else. 
    • Example: According to the menu, a side salad and rolls will accompany the steak.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: When you speak, there are gestures and body language that accompany your words.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • 'Construct' means To build or make something. (किसी वस्‍तु का निर्माण करना, बनाना; रचना)
    • 'Accomplish' means To succeed in doing something difficult that you planned to do. (किसी कठिन कार्य को करने में सफल होना)
    • 'Achieve' means To complete something by hard work and skill. (किसी कार्य को मेहनत व कौशल द्वारा संपन्‍न करना)
       

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य कह रहा है कि जब हम बोलते हैं तो हमारे हाव-भाव हमारे शब्दों के साथ मेल खाते हैं।
  • इसलिए, रिक्त स्थान में भरने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द 'accompany' है।
  • 'Accompany' शब्द का अर्थ है कुछ भी जो किसी और चीज़ के साथ अच्छी तरह मेल खाती हो।
    • उदाहरण: According to the menu, a side salad and rolls will accompany the steak.


अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

पूर्ण वाक्य: When you speak, there are gestures and body language that accompany your words.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with an appropriate option. The _______ of revenge demanded a life for a life.

questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Obligations'. The word "obligations" refers to duties or actions one is bound to perform, either morally or legally. In the context of this sentence, it implies that the code or rules of revenge demand an equal response—in this case, a life for a life. Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'The obligations of revenge demanded a life for a life.'

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Computers would replace the ______ technique of creating an image on paper, transferring it to cells and again onto film.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Computers would replace the ______ technique of creating an image on paper, transferring it to cells and again onto film.
questions.solution: The reason to use "archaic" in the blank is to convey that the technique being described is outdated, old-fashioned, or no longer in common use. Using "archaic" suggests that computers would replace a method that was once employed but is now considered obsolete, especially in the context of image creation and reproduction. Correct sentence: Computers would replace the archaic technique of creating an image on paper, transferring it to cells and again onto film.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. From these findings, we can ______ that the rate of crime is increasing in the city.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

From these findings, we can ______ that the rate of crime is increasing in the city.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'infer.'


Key Points

  • Infer means to form an opinion or decide that something is true from the information you have.

 ​                     -Example: Jack's answers to my questions during our interview allowed me to infer that he was not the right candidate for the position.

So, it is clear that the most appropriate word is 'infer'.

The complete sentence is "From these findings, we can infer that the rate of crime is increasing in the city.".
​

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

Additional Information

  • Presuppose means to accept something as true or existing and act on that basis, before it has been shown to be true.
  • Summarise means to tell in or reduce to a summary.
  • Presume means to think that something is true even if you do not know for sure; to suppose.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Her face was ______ after seeing the house in such condition.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her face was ______ after seeing the house in such condition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. 'Blue'.
Key Points
  • The blank in the sentence requires an adjective which refers to a feeling of sadness or depression.
  • 'Blue' (Option 2) fits this context correctly, as it's an idiom that means feeling sad or depressed (उदास या निराश).
  • So, the filled sentence would be: "Her face was blue after seeing the house in such condition."
Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Blue'.
Additional Information
  • 'Bedew' (Option 1) is a verb which means to wet with or as with dew ('ओस से गीला करना'), which doesn't make sense in this context.
  • 'Brew' (Option 3) can refer to making a hot drink like tea or coffee ('भूनना' or 'पकाना'), or to a plan forming (योजना बना'), but neither fit well here.
  • 'Blew' (Option 4) is the past tense of the verb 'blow' (फूंकना'), and isn't coherent in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The huge vase looks out of ______ with the surroundings.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The huge vase looks out of ______ with the surroundings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1), i.e., 'place.'

Key Points  

  • Let's look at the meaning of the words given in the options:
    Word Meaning
    place a suitable area, building, situation, or occasion. (एक उपयुक्त क्षेत्र, भवन, स्थिति या अवसर)
    size how large or small something or someone is. (कोई चीज या कोई कितना बड़ा या छोटा है)
    design to make or draw plans for something, for example, clothes or buildings. (किसी चीज़ की योजना बनाना या बनाना, उदाहरण के लिए कपड़े या भवन)
    shape the particular physical form or appearance of something. (किसी चीज का विशेष भौतिक रूप या स्वरूप)
  • The context of the sentence is that the extremely large vase doesn't seem suitable for the room.
  • According to the above-mentioned points, the most appropriate word to fill in the blank is "place."
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
  • Another example:
    • Lightning never strikes twice in the same place.
 

Complete Sentence: The huge vase looks out of place with the surroundings.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Doctors and nurses who are treating COVID-19 patients are finding it difficult ______ long working hours.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Doctors and nurses who are treating COVID-19 patients are finding it difficult ______ long working hours.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To cope with'

Key Points

  • Let's see the meanings of the given words-
    • Carry on- continue an activity or task. (एक गतिविधि या कार्य जारी रखें।)
    • Service for- the action of helping or doing work for someone. (किसी की मदद करने या काम करने की क्रिया।)
    • Cope with- (of a person) deal effectively with something difficult. ((किसी व्यक्ति का) किसी कठिन कार्य से प्रभावी ढंग से निपटना।)
    • Manage with-  To be able to operate, function, or carry on adequately with a smaller amount of people or things than one had anticipated. (एक से कम लोगों या चीजों के साथ पर्याप्त रूप से संचालित करने, कार्य करने या पर्याप्त रूप से चलाने में सक्षम होने के लिए।)
  • Hence, according to the meanings of the phrases, the correct answer is Option 3 i.e. to cope with.

So the correct sentence is- Doctors and nurses who are treating COVID-19 patients are finding it difficult to cope with long working hours.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Words such as articles and pronouns can be ______ unless they are necessary.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Words such as articles and pronouns can be ______ unless they are necessary.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'dropped.'

Key Points 

  • Let's look at the meaning of the words given in the options:
    Word Meaning
    disbarred to make someone unable to continue working as a lawyer, especially because they have done something wrong. (किसी को वकील के रूप में काम करना जारी रखने में असमर्थ बनाने के लिए, खासकर इसलिए क्योंकि उन्होंने कुछ गलत किया है)
    disrupted to prevent something, especially a system, process, or event, from continuing as usual or as expected. (किसी चीज़, विशेष रूप से एक प्रणाली, प्रक्रिया, या घटना को सामान्य या अपेक्षित रूप से जारी रखने से रोकने के लिए)
    dispelled to remove fears, doubts, and false ideas, usually by proving them wrong or unnecessary. (to remove fears, doubts, and false ideas, usually by proving them wrong or unnecessary)
    dropped to fall or to allow something to fall; to stop including someone or something. (गिरना या किसी चीज को गिरने देना; किसी को या कुछ शामिल करना बंद करना)
 
  • The context of the sentence is that we should not include unnecessary articles and pronouns in a sentence.
  • According to the above-mentioned points, the most appropriate word to fill in the blank is "dropped."
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
  • Another example:
    • Peter threw his feet over the wagon seat and dropped to the ground.
 

Complete Sentence: Words such as articles and pronouns can be dropped unless they are necessary.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The shops at the Indian airports have to ______ prices in Indian rupees.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for the given blank. Changing his tactics he tried to ________ him and offered him money.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

Changing his tactics he tried to ________ him and offered him money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "bribe" means to persuade someone to act in one's favor, typically illegally or dishonestly, by a gift of money or other inducements. (रिश्वत देना)
    • Example: He tried to bribe the official to get his work done quickly.
  • "Bribe" refers to the act of giving someone money or other inducements to act in one's favor. (रिश्वत देना)
    • Example: They attempted to bribe the guard to let them through the gate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Bribed (रिश्वत दी): The past tense of 'bribe'.
    • Example: He bribed the officer to avoid a ticket.
  • Bribing (रिश्वत देना): The present participle of 'bribe'.
    • Example: Bribing officials is illegal and punishable by law.
  • Be bribe (रिश्वत होना): Incorrect form for the context provided.
    • Example: This phrase does not fit grammatically in the given sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As he went through the street on an ________ that morning, he saw a woman with a cat under her arm.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As he went through the street on an ________ that morning, he saw a woman with a cat under her arm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, "errand."

Key Points

  • An "errand" refers to a short trip taken to perform a specific task or job, often on behalf of someone else.
  • In the given sentence, the person is walking through the street on an errand, which suggests that they have a specific task to accomplish.
  • Option 1, "objection," refers to a disagreement or protest, and does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
  • Option 2, "encasement," refers to the act of enclosing something in a protective covering or container, which also does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
  • Option 4, "amendment," refers to a change or addition made to a document or law, and does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.


Correct Sentence: As he went through the street on an errand that morning, he saw a woman with a cat under her arm.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank. The air-conditioner has made ceiling fans a little ______ in today's world.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.

The air-conditioner has made ceiling fans a little ______ in today's world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. Redundant.

Key Points

  • Meanings of the given options are:
    • Extinct means having no living members. (कोई जीवित सदस्य नहीं होना।)
    • Redundant means no longer needed or useful; superfluous. (अब इसकी आवश्यकता या उपयोगी नहीं है; ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा)
    • Additional means added, extra, or supplementary to what is already present or available. (जो पहले से मौजूद या उपलब्ध है उसमें जोड़ा, अतिरिक्त या पूरक)
    • Absurd means unreasonable, illogical, or inappropriate. (अनुचित, अतार्किक या अनुचित)
  • The given sentence is about the effect of air-conditioners on the use of ceiling fans.
  • Hence the correct answer is 'redundant'.

Correct sentence: The air-conditioner has made ceiling fans a little redundant in today's world.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank The man who is supposed to be protecting them is somehow their fiercest and most ______ enemy.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank

The man who is supposed to be protecting them is somehow their fiercest and most ______ enemy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "implacable".

Key Points

  • The word 'implacable'  (अटल) accurately conveys the relentless and unstoppable nature of the enemy. This would be the suitable choice to indicate the gravity and fierce character of the enemy mentioned here.
  • Words like 'pedestrian', 'ostentatious', and 'quotidian' do not express the severity or intensity of the enemy's character.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Additional Information

  • "Implacable" (अटल): This word means unable to be placated or unstoppable, often used referring to an enemy or a critic. In the sentence, it conveys the relentless and persistent nature of the enemy. 
  • "Pedestrian"(पैदल चलने वाला): When this term isn't referring to a person walking along a road or in a developed area, it means lacking inspiration or excitement; dull. In the context of the sentence, we can deduce it would not be the correct word to use, since it does not represent the fierceness of the enemy.
  • "Ostentatious"(दिखावटी): This word means showy, grand, or flamboyant and is usually used to describe something that wants to attract attention. An enemy can be ostentatious, however, in this context, it seems the enemy's primary quality needs to be his relentlessness, not his flashiness. Hence, this wouldn't be an appropriate fit for the blank.
  • "Quotidian"(प्रतिदिन का, दैनिक): This word refers to something that is daily or ordinary. Again, it does not fit the context of the sentence that mentions a "fiercest" enemy, which implies a character that is extraordinary and ruthless in some way.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. By accelerating digitisation and leveraging next-generation technologies, the life insurance sector can double its ______ to Rupees 70 lakh crores, a study said.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. Her mother is a wonderful host, she prepared for us a seven ________ meal all by herself.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Her mother is a wonderful host, she prepared for us a seven ________ meal all by herself.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "course" (option 2). In the context of a meal, "course" refers to a particular part of a meal sequence, such as an appetizer, main dish, or dessert. The word "coarse" (option 3) means rough or crude, and "coarser" (option 1) is the comparative form of "coarse." "Courser" (option 4) is not relevant here.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most suitable word. In addition, it is believed they possess crude electronic devices capable of triggering ______ bombs.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

In addition, it is believed they possess crude electronic devices capable of triggering ______ bombs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. 'Incendiary'. 

Additional Information

  • The word "incendiary" refers to something related to setting fire or causing fires. (आगजनक)
  • In the given sentence, it is believed that they possess crude electronic devices capable of triggering bombs.
  • The word "incendiary" fits well as it suggests the devices have the potential to cause explosions or fires.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'In addition, it is believed they possess crude electronic devices capable of triggering incendiary bombs. 

Additional Information

  • Explanation of other options:
    • Insipid: "Insipid" means lacking flavor or taste. It does not make sense in the context of triggering bombs. (बेस्वाद)
    • Intelligible: "Intelligible" means capable of being understood or clear. It does not fit the context of explosive devices or triggering bombs. (समझने योग्य)
    • Insensible: "Insensible" means lacking awareness or consciousness. It does not relate to the capability of triggering bombs. (मूर्ख)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. However, even after Independence in 1947, British expatriate firms did not suddenly ___________ from India.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

However, even after Independence in 1947, British expatriate firms did not suddenly ___________ from India.
questions.solution:
"The correct answer is option 3, "divest."

Key Points

  • To divest means to sell off or get rid of something, often referring to a company or organization selling off assets or investments.
  • In the context of the sentence, it means that British expatriate firms did not suddenly sell off or get rid of their businesses in India after Independence in 1947.
    • Example: The company decided to divest its non-core assets to focus on its main business.
  • Option 1, "close," means to shut down or cease operations. In the context of the sentence, it would mean that British expatriate firms shut down their businesses in India after Independence.
    • Example: The restaurant had to close due to a lack of customers.
  • Option 2, "disallow," means to forbid or prohibit something. In the context of the sentence, it does not make sense as British expatriate firms were not forbidden or prohibited from operating in India after Independence.
    • Example: The teacher disallowed the use of calculators during the exam.
  • Option 4, "consecrate," means to make something sacred or holy. In the context of the sentence, it does not make sense as British expatriate firms were not made sacred or holy in India after Independence.
    • Example: The church was consecrated by the bishop.
  • Overall, option 3, "divest," is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence.


Correct Sentence: However, even after Independence in 1947, British expatriate firms did not suddenly divest from India.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. This ______ piece of mischief by his brother brought a quiet laugh from David.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This ______ piece of mischief by his brother brought a quiet laugh from David.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'Whimsical'.
Key Points
  • The sentence is looking for an adjective to describe 'mischief'.
  • Therefore, the suitable option should align with the context of 'mischief', which is usually lighthearted or playful wrongdoing.
  • The word 'whimsical' perfectly fits in this context. It means playfully quaint or fanciful, particularly in an appealing and amusing way.
  • The mischief causing 'a quiet laugh' aligns with this notion.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'This whimsical piece of mischief by his brother brought a quiet laugh from David'.

Additional Information

  • 'Nonsensical' could imply the mischief was meaningless or absurd, but it does not necessarily indicate the mischievous act was amusing or responsible for David's laugh.
  • 'Classical' implies that the mischief is conventional, traditional, or long-established. It does not fit well with the tiny act of mischief described in the sentence.
  • 'Vesical' refers to the bladder or a bladder-like structure, which does not make sense in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blanks. Advocates say the idea of a basic income eliminates poverty traps and _____ income while _____the individual and reducing paperwork.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blanks.

Advocates say the idea of a basic income eliminates poverty traps and _____ income while _____the individual and reducing paperwork.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is redistributes; empowering.

Key Points

  • The sentence is in the Present tense thus eliminating option 2 (earned - past tense).
  • The idea of Basic income is taking the profits of the PSU's and giving it to the poor. So, the income is 'redistributed' (i.e. from PSU's to the poor ).
  • Basic income will help them come out of poverty traps and instill confidence in the poor thus 'empowering' them (empower - make (someone) stronger and more confident)
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.
     

The correct sentence is: Advocates say the idea of a basic income eliminates poverty traps and redistributes income while empowering the individual and reducing paperwork.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ yourself with the new perfume.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

______ yourself with the new perfume.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Pamper.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is saying to do something with the new perfume. (दिया गया वाक्य नए परफ्यूम के साथ कुछ करने के लिए कह रहा है)
  • Pamper means indulging with every attention, comfort, and kindness. (संतुष्ट करना)
    • Example: Pamper yourself with a stay in one of our luxury hotels.
       

Conclusion: To enjoy the availability or use of the new perfume. (अपने आप को नए इत्र के साथ संतुष्ट करना)

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: Pamper yourself with the new perfume.

Mistake Points

  • You may think that 'purify' can be the correct answer but it is not true. (आप सोच सकते हैं कि 'purify' सही उत्तर हो सकता है लेकिन यह सच नहीं है)
  • A perfume does not purify us. (एक इत्र हमें शुद्ध नहीं करता है)
  • Thus, 'pamper' is the correct answer.


Additional Information

  • Let us explore the other options:
    • Prosper means to develop in a successful way; to be successful, especially with money. (सफलतापूर्वक विकसित होना; धन की दृष्टि से समृद्घ होना)
    • Percolate means to move gradually through a surface that has very small holes or spaces in it. (छोटे छिद्रों से रिसना या बहना)
    • Purify means to remove dirty or harmful substances from something. (किसी वस्‍तु को शुद्घ या साफ़ करना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Raghav had a good ______ for stage plays.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Raghav had a good ______ for stage plays.
questions.solution: Troupe is a group of actors or performers who work together regularly. It is the most appropriate option to fill the blank, as it fits the context of stage plays. Example: Raghav joined a troupe of actors to perform in the local theatre production.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The driver very subtly ______ the traffic violation he committed.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The driver very subtly ______ the traffic violation he committed.
questions.solution: "Ironed-out" is a commonly used expression that means to resolve, smooth out, or eliminate difficulties or problems. Example: After a brief discussion, they successfully ironed-out the differences and reached a compromise. It is often used in the context of negotiations or discussions to reach an agreement or understanding. In the sentence, the phrase "ironed-out" is used metaphorically. In this context, it suggests that the driver skillfully and discreetly resolved or smoothed over the consequences of the traffic violation.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate itby selecting the appropriate option. Rohan and Sohan are brothers but the ______ is very poor.

In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate itby selecting the appropriate option.

Rohan and Sohan are brothers but the ______ is very poor.
questions.solution: The only word that makes sense here is ‘latter’ which means ‘denoting the second or second mentioned of two people or things.’ The other words cannot fit here. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal __________ Committee in many nations.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal __________ Committee in many nations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Ethics'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "Ethics" refers to the moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
  • In the context of animal welfare, an Ethics Committee is established to ensure that the treatment of animals is aligned with ethical standards.
  • The other options: "Resistant," "Considers," and "Customs" do not fit the context or convey the appropriate meaning.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Complete Sentence: The rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal Ethics Committee in many nations.

Additional Information
  • Resistant (प्रतिरोधी): means able to withstand or oppose.
  • Considers (विचार करता है): means to think carefully about.
  • Customs (रीति रिवाज): means traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The order was quickly ______ in the area after the scuffle between the two groups.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

The order was quickly ______ in the area after the scuffle between the two groups.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'restored'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is talking about something that happened with the order after the scuffle.
  • The use of the word 'scuffle' in the sentence indicates a physical dispute between the two groups.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'restored'.
  • 'Restored' means to bring back someone or something to a former condition, place, or position.
    • Example: The clock was restored to its original condition.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: The order was quickly restored in the area after the scuffle between the two groups.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore the other options:
    • 'Rebuilt' means to build something again after it has been damaged or destroyed.
    • 'Repaired' means to restore something damaged, faulty, or worn to a good condition.
    • 'Recovered' means to find or regain possession of something stolen or lost.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. For many, The Lion King is _____ as a childhood memory.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

For many, The Lion King is _____ as a childhood memory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.

  • Treasured: cherished, value highly
  • Invested: put in financial schemes, property; 
  • Inherited: received as an heir at the death of the previous holder; derived genetically from one's parents or ancestors
  • Deposited: put or set down something in a specific place; pay a sum

Other words do not make the sentence meaningful.

The correct sentence will be: For many, The Lion King is cherished as a childhood memory.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ravi has little in _____________ with his friend, Senthil.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Ravi has little in _____________ with his friend, Senthil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. common.

Key Points

  • The word "common" means something that is shared by two or more people or things. (साझा / सामान्य)
    • Example: They have many interests in common, which makes their friendship strong.
  • The context tells us that Ravi and his friend, Senthil, share very few similarities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: common.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Contention (विवाद): A heated disagreement or argument.
    • Example: There was much contention between the two teams over the referee's decision.
  • Formal (औपचारिक): Following established conventions or rules.
    • Example: The meeting was conducted in a very formal manner.
  • Normal (सामान्य): Conforming to a standard; usual, typical, or expected.
    • Example: It is normal to feel nervous before an exam.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was laughing from the ______ exuberance of the performance.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She was laughing from the ______ exuberance of the performance.
questions.solution: Sheer: not mixed with anything else; pure or complete. It is an adjective used to create emphasis. Example: It was a moment of sheer bliss for his family and friends when he crossed the finishing line of the marathon.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Our professor speaks English with a ______ Oriya accent.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

Our professor speaks English with a ______ Oriya accent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'pronounced'. 

Key Points

  • The most appropriate word for the given fill in the blank is 'pronounced'. 
  • Let's look at the meaning and examples of the given options:
    • Widespread existing or happening in many places and/or among many people There are reports of widespread flooding in northern France.
      Vague not clearly expressed, known, described, or decided The patient had complained of vague pains and backache.
      Pronounced very noticeable or certain/ easily noticeable; obvious She's a woman of very pronounced views which she is not afraid to air.
      Remarkable unusual or special and therefore surprising and worth mentioning Nelson Mandela was a truly remarkable man.
    • By reading the above definitions, we find that the correct answer is 'pronounced'. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3. 
    ​

Complete sentence: Our professor speaks English with a pronounced Oriya accent.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence. He had his own line of thinking and would defend his views with ______.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.

He had his own line of thinking and would defend his views with ______.
questions.solution: The word 'conviction' means a firmly held belief or opinion. So, as he had his line of thinking, he defended his views. So, 'conviction' is the correct word.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word. It is said that Man has ______ almost twenty different animals to make them serve his own needs.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.

It is said that Man has ______ almost twenty different animals to make them serve his own needs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is tamed.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meanings of the given options: 
    • tamed- make less powerful and easier to control
    • tutored- act as a tutor to (a single student or a very small group)
    • tricked- deceive or outwit (someone) by being cunning or skillful
    • pushed- hold and exert force on (something) so as to cause it to move along in front of one
  • As per the context of the sentence, humans have controlled around 20 distinct animals for their own use.
  • Hence, from the given meanings, we find that the 1st option i.e. tamed is the correct choice.
     

​Correct Sentence: It is said that Man has tamed almost twenty different animals to make them serve his own needs.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. In the age of technology, sending letters by postal mail seems __________ to me.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.
In the age of technology, sending letters by postal mail seems __________ to me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. 'superfluous'.

'Superfluous' Refers to something that is unnecessary.

The sentence means that in the times of technology, sending messages by post is unnecessary.

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

  • Superstition: Refers to a belief that is respectful of the supernatural
  • Surplus: Refers to something that is more than what is needed, something that is in excess
  • Supercilious: Refers to someone who thinks or looks as though they are superior to others. 

 

Thus, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Although I was _________ of his new plans for the growth of the company, I relied on him as he was very honest.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Although I was _________ of his new plans for the growth of the company, I relied on him as he was very honest.
questions.solution: skeptical: doubtful. The word 'although' means 'in spite of the fact'. Clearly, the given clauses are contrasting with each other. Hence, 'skeptical' is the only word which fit here well.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If the anesthesia is not ______ properly, he might wake up in the ______ of the surgery.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

If the anesthesia is not ______  properly, he might wake up in the ______ of the surgery.
questions.solution: To complete the sentence meaningfully, the word "administered" fits best in the first blank, as anesthesia needs to be administered properly. The word "middle" is appropriate for the second blank, indicating the patient might wake up during the surgery. Therefore, option 4 is the most suitable.
